---
title: Described tool results
description: describedResult() — a tool returns rows, a series or relationships as typed data, with grain, freshness and coverage traveling with the numbers; a build gate refuses a triage tool that forgets its caveats, by name.
---

> Your inventory tool reports `jobs_local: 331` and `jobs_replicated_in: 607`. The model adds them and announces 938 protected jobs — a fleet nobody has, because those two numbers must never be summed. The tool's author knew that. The knowledge lived in a comment. **`describedResult()` makes the caveats typed data that travel with the values**, and `check:semantics` is the build gate that refuses a tool that forgot them.

## The problem: honesty by culture

The conventions that make tool answers trustworthy — grain stated, counters marked, freshness declared, "not covered" named on every triage — get re-implemented by hand inside every tool and held in place by code review. That scales to one disciplined author. It does not scale to a hundred tools or to adapters written by other teams.

`describedResult()` turns the conventions into construction. Every value in the declaration comes from the data — here the export's own timestamp is `measuredAt`:

<CodeFile path="examples/features/66-semantic-envelope.ts" region="described-result" title="examples/features/66-semantic-envelope.ts (region: described-result)" />

The declaration is camelCase; the envelope the model and the record read is snake_case, and never changes:

| field | what it says | on the wire |
|---|---|---|
| `series` | measured points — `{ t, entity, metric, value }` | `series` |
| `facts` | typed rows about entities — every row names its `entity` | `facts` |
| `edges` | typed relationships — `{ from, to, kind }` | `edges` |
| `grain` | what one value MEANS: `interval`, `aggregation`, `isCounter`, `collapsed` | `grain`, with `is_counter` |
| `provenance` | `measuredAt` (when the WORLD was measured — not when the tool ran), `source`, `ageSeconds`, `sourceExportDate` | `provenance`, with `measured_at`, `age_seconds`, `source_export_date` |
| `period` | what time the READ behind the data covered: `queried` (the instants it asked for), `held` (what the store holds, or `'unknown'`), `readAt` — ISO 8601 instants with a zone; the results layer files its verdict ([The period a result covered](doc:tools#the-period-a-result-covered--period)) | `period`, with `read_at` — served to the model as declared |
| `coverage` | the three-list vocabulary `coverage()` and `absent()` speak: `checked`, `notChecked`, `cannotCover` | `coverage` (`not_checked`, `cannot_cover`) and the `not_covered` lines composed from it |
| `clarify` | the ask-vs-answer decision as data: `{ question, candidates }`, or `null` for "ambiguity considered, none found" | `clarify` |
| `render` | hints for a UI — `default`, `columns`, `sort`, `filterNote`, `chartHint`; the model never sees them | `render`, with `filter_note`, `chart_hint` |

`isCounter` means a cumulative reading a reader must never add up: a total since the job was created. One day's count of successful runs is not a counter — adding days gives the week's total — so the example states `isCounter: false`. Either way it must be stated when `aggregation` is counter-looking (`sum`, `count`, `total`, `cumulative`, `counter`, `delta`).

`describedResult()` refuses at the call site — the `absent()` law — anything the vocabulary cannot honor: series without `grain`, series or facts without `provenance.measuredAt` and `provenance.source`, a counter-looking aggregation with `isCounter` unstated. A missing `provenance` beside `series` or `facts` is also a compile error. A key the declaration — or its `grain`, `provenance`, `coverage`, `clarify` or `render` — does not have is refused too, never dropped, and a snake_case key names the camelCase one meant (`provenance.measured_at` → "did you mean `measuredAt`?"). Inside `execute` a refusal becomes the call's error result, which is what the model reads, so it starts `refused:` and names the field as you spelled it: `refused: this result carries series/facts with no provenance — provenance.measuredAt and provenance.source are required…`.

## Where it lives

```text
  execute() returns describedResult({ … })
          │   nothing is added to the system prompt or the tool's schema
          │
          ├─▶ the tool message ─── what the MODEL reads: the data, grain,
          │                        provenance, one not_covered line per gap,
          │                        a non-null clarify, the static note
          │
          ├─▶ the run record ───── tools.semantics_declared: the WHOLE envelope
          │                        (checked list, render hints, marker) and the
          │                        coverage rows in coverageDeclared
          │
          └─▶ the final answer ─── only with .limitsTravelWithTheAnswer(): the
                                   coverage lists, appended — never provenance
                                   or grain
```

- **It is the tool's response.** Nothing goes into the system prompt or the tool spec; the envelope is the value `execute` returns.
- **The model reads a projection**, `semanticsForModel`: the data, `grain`, `provenance`, a declared `period` as declared, the `not_covered` lines composed from `coverage` (never hand-written, so the two cannot disagree), a non-null `clarify`, and a static note telling it how to read the caveats. It does NOT read the `checked` list, the `render` hints or the `af_semantics` marker. (`absent()` and `coverage()` do serve their `checked` lists — see [what each helper serves](doc:tools#what-execute-returns--three-helpers-one-rule).)
- **The record keeps everything**, on the typed `agentfootprint.tools.semantics_declared` event — one per recognized envelope, stamped with the tool name, the tool call id and the iteration — and the coverage lands in `sharedState.coverageDeclared` beside every `coverage()` and `absent()` statement. The event is emitted **before** the tool's `resultCeiling` is measured, so an oversized result that is refused still leaves its grain and provenance on the record.
- **Only coverage reaches the final answer**, and only with [`.limitsTravelWithTheAnswer()`](doc:tools#making-the-limits-survive--limitstravelwiththeanswer). Provenance and grain are for the model and the record.
- **A fact without a source never reaches the model.** It is refused inside the tool; the model reads the refusal in its place, and the run continues.
- **An empty list is not "nothing matched".** `series`, `facts` and `edges` are never empty, so a found branch cannot also be the not-found branch: `describedResult({ facts: [] })` is refused with `` `facts` is empty — if nothing matched, return absent({ what, checked }) instead ``. Write both: `rows.length ? describedResult({ … }) : absent({ … })`. `check:semantics` says the same about a sample that exercises the empty branch.
- **`measuredAt` is never parsed.** It is the tool's own words for a time — `"last year, roughly"` passes — and it rides to the model as written.

```ts
agent.on('agentfootprint.tools.semantics_declared', (e) => {
  e.payload.semantics; // the FULL envelope — render hints, coverage, all of it
});
```

It lands in recordings (`recordRun` / `persistRecording`), so a UI can draw the table the author hinted at months after the run.

**Composition:** the result envelopes stack. `{ content: describedResult({...}), effects: [...], status: 'partial' }` is one result that carries typed data AND a [tool effect](doc:tools) AND an outcome status. `absent()` remains the answer for "I looked and found nothing"; never wrap a described result in `coverage()` — it carries its own.

## Values from the data

`measuredAt` is when the world was measured, and the data knows when that was. Take it from the data; never type a date into a tool:

| the result | `measuredAt` is |
|---|---|
| rows from an export or a nightly file | the export's own timestamp |
| a live read | the moment of the read — take `new Date().toISOString()` when you query |
| a series | the newest sample's time |
| a value computed over a window ("the last 24h") | the END of the window |

`ageSeconds` is how old that was when the tool answered. It must be a finite number ≥ 0, so compute it only from a time you can parse — for an ISO export time, `Math.max(0, Math.round((Date.now() - Date.parse(exportedAt)) / 1000))` — and leave it out otherwise; `measuredAt` still says when.

A computed result is still data from its system of record — a count over the export's rows carries the export's provenance:

```ts
const failed = runs.filter((r) => r.ok === 0);
return describedResult({
  facts: [{ entity: vm, failed_runs: failed.length, runs_seen: runs.length }],
  provenance: { measuredAt: snapshot.exportedAt, source: snapshot.source },
});
```

A clarify-only result hands the question back instead of picking silently; it needs no provenance:

```ts
const matches = customers.filter((c) => c.name.startsWith(query));
if (matches.length > 1) {
  return describedResult({
    clarify: {
      question: `${matches.length} customers match "${query}" — which one?`,
      candidates: matches.map((c) => c.name),
    },
  });
}
```

`clarify` does **not** pause the run: the model reads the question and decides what to do with it — often, to ask the person in its answer. To stop the run until a person supplies a value, use [`requestInput()`](doc:input-requests).

## check:semantics — the build gate

The gate judges **sample results** (what your mock tools return — a build must never run tools that touch live systems) against the envelope rules and the per-class rules declared on `defineTool({ resultClass })`:

| rule | severity |
|---|---|
| `'triage'` result with no coverage declaration (a described result's `coverage`, `coverage()`, or `absent()`) | error |
| `'inventory'` result with no coverage declaration | error |
| marker-bearing envelope with faults: `series-without-grain`, `data-without-provenance`, `counter-aggregation-unstated`, `malformed-semantics` | error |
| `'inventory'` with `facts` but no `render` hint | warning |
| a classed tool with zero sample results | warning |

Severity follows provability: only what the declarations prove wrong errors. Every finding names the **tool** and the **field**, and a missing coverage tells the author to return `describedResult({ …, coverage })`, `coverage(result, …)` or `absent({ … })`.

Wire it beside your other gates (the `check:tools` convention) — dump `[{ name, resultClass, results: [...] }]` to JSON and:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "check:semantics": "agentfootprint-check-semantics semantics-catalog.json"
  }
}
```

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` findings failed the gate (`--strict` gates warnings too), `2` input error. The same core is callable in-process:

```ts
import { checkSemantics, formatSemanticsReport } from 'agentfootprint/observe';

const report = checkSemantics([
  { name: 'vm_backup_status', resultClass: 'triage', results: [sampleResult] },
]);
if (!report.ok) throw new Error(formatSemanticsReport(report));
```

## Zero-cost when unused

Recognition is strict: only a plain object whose `af_semantics` is exactly `true` **and** that passes the whole rule set is an envelope. Every other value any tool has ever returned — including a marker-bearing shape with faults, which is dev-warned and named by the gate but never half-applied — takes the exact path it always took, byte for byte.

## Migration from the removed declaration door

The deprecated `semantic()` function and `SemanticDeclaration` type have been
removed. Use `describedResult()` and `DescribedResultDeclaration`. In declarations,
rename `is_counter` → `isCounter`, `measured_at` → `measuredAt`,
`age_seconds` → `ageSeconds`, `source_export_date` → `sourceExportDate`,
`filter_note` → `filterNote` and `chart_hint` → `chartHint`. Coverage
declarations already use `notChecked` and `cannotCover`; keep those names.
Series and facts require provenance in the declaration type as well as at runtime.

Do **not** rename keys in saved records or foreign-language wire envelopes:
`ToolSemantics`, its snake_case fields, the marker, note and model projection
are unchanged. `readSemantics()` continues to recognize valid saved envelopes.

## Vocabulary reference

The authoring half ships on the main barrel (`agentfootprint`). `describedResult` is the single authoring door and mints the envelope from a `DescribedResultDeclaration`. The rendered value is a `ToolSemantics` carrying `SemanticSeriesPoint` rows, `SemanticFact` rows, `SemanticEdge` links, a `SemanticGrain`, a `SemanticProvenance`, a `SemanticCoverage` (whose derived `not_covered` lines are composed by `composeNotCovered`), a `SemanticClarify` question and `SemanticRender` hints. `readSemantics` is the strict recognizer the dispatch loop uses; `explainSemantics` names the faults — `SemanticIssue` rows, each with a `SemanticIssueCode` — on a marker-bearing value that was not recognized; `semanticsForModel` builds the model's compact projection; `isCounterLookingAggregation` and the `COUNTER_AGGREGATION_WORDS` list decide when `is_counter` must be stated. The marker key is `SEMANTICS_MARKER` (the string `af_semantics`), the static note text is `SEMANTICS_NOTE`, the closed class set is `RESULT_CLASSES` (typed as `ToolResultClass`), and `assertResultClass` is the definition-time refusal `defineTool` runs on a declared class.

`SEMANTICS_NOTE` and `SEMANTICS_MARKER` are also published as **data**, beside the coverage/absence notes, at `node_modules/agentfootprint/canonical-notes.json` — for a tool written in a language that cannot import them. See [reading the canonical notes from another language](doc:tools#reading-the-canonical-notes-from-another-language-9700).

The gate half ships on `agentfootprint/observe`. `checkSemantics` judges an array of `SemanticsCatalogEntry` rows and returns a `SemanticsReport` of `SemanticsFinding` rows, each carrying a `SemanticsFindingCode`, the tool and the field; `formatSemanticsReport` renders the report for a terminal; `coerceSemanticsCatalog` normalizes the accepted JSON shapes; and `runCheckSemanticsCli` is the unit-testable CLI core behind the `agentfootprint-check-semantics` bin, with its IO injected through `SemanticsCliIO`.
